clue.text: Write back irregularly, or send promptly at first?

indicators.note: irregularly tells us the letters are set in no fixed order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word promptly

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to answer letters now and then or dash off a quick reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irregularly' shuffles OR, SEND and P (the first letter of 'promptly', signalled by 'at first') into RESPOND.
explanation.definitionFit: To respond is to reply, and writing back to someone is replying to them.

clue.text: Polish, English or American country bumpkin?

parts.note: to polish is to rub

explanation.surface: Asks the nationality of a country yokel: Polish, English or American?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' wants to be a nationality; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Rube is American slang for an unsophisticated rural person, a hick.

clue.text: Take adjustable lens to capture timeless Welsh river

indicators.note: to capture says one piece holds another inside
adjustable signals the letters of lens can be altered into another order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: timeless removes T, the abbreviation for time

parts.note: the Taff is a river in South Wales flowing through Cardiff

explanation.surface: A photographer fits a zoom lens to shoot a Welsh river.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh river is the Taff, which flows through Cardiff; 'adjustable' shuffles LENS to SNLE, which then holds AFF.
explanation.definitionFit: To snaffle something is informal British for taking it, often sneakily.

clue.text: Appearance of Durham town, apart from its outskirts

indicators.note: apart from its outskirts says the town's outer letters are dropped

parts.note: Consett is a former steel town in County Durham

explanation.surface: The look of a northern English town, excluding its suburbs.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the first and last letters of CONSETT. 'Appearance' means arrival, not looks.
explanation.definitionFit: The onset of something is its beginning or first appearance, as of an illness.

clue.text: Severe upset for Jack, perhaps — coin's counterfeit

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the word over so it reads from the bottom

parts.note: a jack is one example of a playing card

indicators.note: counterfeit suggests the letters are faked into a false arrangement

parts.note: the letters of coin, the possessive adding nothing

explanation.surface: A man called Jack is distressed that his coin turns out to be fake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns CARD into DRAC; 'counterfeit' rearranges COIN into ONIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Draconic means extremely harsh, after Draco, the Athenian lawgiver of famously severe laws.

clue.text: One singing shanty originally needed to raise pitch

parts.note: to jack something is to raise it, as with a car jack
tar is pitch, the black sticky stuff

explanation.surface: A sea-song singer must first lift the key of the tune.
explanation.walkthrough: JACK TAR is an old name for a sailor, the sort who once sang shanties; 'pitch' looks musical but is the black substance.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jack tar is a traditional name for a seaman, and sea shanties were sung by sailors at work.

clue.text: Family taking exercise outside, but not serious

indicators.note: outside says the exercise word goes round the family word

parts.note: to jog is to take exercise
kin are family members

explanation.surface: Relatives go running together, just for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' is only a link: 'outside' alone is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone joking is speaking in jest, so they are not being serious.

clue.text: A feat performed with rice in restaurant

indicators.note: performed suggests the letters are worked into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone pulls off a stunt with rice in a diner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performed' rearranges A, FEAT and RICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafeteria is a self-service restaurant.

clue.text: One about to join in games taken up in hot regions

indicators.note: to join in says the pieces go into the middle of another word
taken up in a down clue means the word is read upwards

parts.note: sport is games
one is the Roman numeral I
c is circa, about

explanation.surface: A single player is about to take part in sports in the heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' turns SPORT into TROPS, as a down clue reads upward; the C is circa, the Latin for about.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropics are the hot regions of the earth lying around the equator.

clue.text: A football manager might become a wreck

definitions.meaning: read as ..., what a manager of a club might do
a ship that strikes the shore and is stranded

explanation.definitionFit: A ship that runs aground is stranded and may be wrecked; a football manager may run a stadium.

clue.text: Tables turned with an end to rock climber

indicators.note: turned shows the letters of the words before it are turned about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: end to points to the last letter of the word rock

explanation.surface: The tables are turned as a rock climber finally reaches the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' rearranges TABLES and AN into BEANSTAL; 'end to' adds K, the last letter of 'rock'. 'Tables turned' looks like an idiom, but it is the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A beanstalk is a climbing plant, and climber is a standard word for a plant that climbs.

clue.text: For love lost, have gloomy expression

indicators.note: lost says the letter given by love goes missing from the word before it

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O
to own something is to have it

explanation.surface: Someone who has lost the person they love looks downcast.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is nil in tennis, hence O; 'have' supplies the verb own, and the definition is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A frown is a facial look of displeasure or worry, a gloomy expression.

clue.text: Rendered incapable in fortnight of exercises

indicators.note: exercises suggests the letters are put through their paces and worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two weeks of hard training have left someone completely worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercises' rearranges the thirteen letters of IN, FORTNIGHT and OF.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fit for nothing is too exhausted or useless to do anything, so incapable.

clue.text: Manage to find senior politician to support bill

indicators.note: to support in a down clue puts the politician beneath the bill, holding it up

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a bill
a minister is a senior politician in government

explanation.surface: To get something done, have a cabinet member back the proposed law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' looks parliamentary but is a poster. 'to support' puts MINISTER below AD.
explanation.definitionFit: To administer an organisation is to manage or run it.

clue.text: Type of leather said to be expensive swindle

indicators.note: said to be signals that the words are heard spoken, not seen written

parts.note: dear means expensive and a skin is a swindle, as in skinning someone of their money

explanation.surface: Some leather is said to be a costly con.
explanation.walkthrough: DEAR SKIN, a pricey rip-off, sounds like DEERSKIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Deerskin is the hide of a deer, tanned to make a kind of leather.

clue.text: Almost having had enough, say, chap tucked into split

indicators.note: tucked into puts the pieces inside the other word
almost cuts the last letter off the word

parts.note: sated means having had one's fill
eg means for example, say
Reg is a man's name, a chap

explanation.surface: Someone nearly full, with a man tucking in, is ready to break up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' leaves SATE; 'chap' is a generic man's name, a common crossword device.
explanation.definitionFit: To segregate is to separate or split groups apart.

clue.text: Painting fresh coat, hence removing lid

indicators.note: removing says the letters of the hat are taken out of the words before

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
lid is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: Before painting, a new coat is applied after taking the lid off the tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing' takes H, A and T (lid is slang for a hat) out of FRESHCOAT, in that order, leaving FRESCO. 'lid' looks like the paint tin's top.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresco is a painting made on wet plaster, so it is one type of painting.

clue.text: Test sphere holding hydrogen to be put on back burner

indicators.note: holding says the pieces around enclose another letter

parts.note: the MOT is the annual British roadworthiness test for cars
a ball is a sphere
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: A test ball containing hydrogen is to be shelved for now.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is the yearly British vehicle check; the definition reads 'to be put on back burner', with 'to be' as link.
explanation.definitionFit: To mothball a project is to shelve it for later, idiomatically putting it on the back burner.

clue.text: Voguish, like duck's colour

parts.note: in means fashionable, voguish
to dig something is slang for liking it
a duck in cricket is a score of nought, the letter O

explanation.surface: A fashion writer calls a shade trendy, like a duck's plumage.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a score of zero in cricket, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a deep blue-violet shade, one of the colours of the rainbow.

clue.text: Slight colour arising over first part of titillating play

indicators.note: over here means covering, with the reversed word going round the letter
arising in a down clue means reading the word upwards

parts.note: red is a colour

indicators.note: first part of points to the opening letter of the word titillating

parts.note: an act is a part of a play, or to act is to play

explanation.surface: A small colouring rises over the start of a racy show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arising' turns RED into DER, and 'over' wraps it round T (the first letter of 'titillating').
explanation.definitionFit: To slight someone is to belittle them, and detract means to belittle or diminish.

clue.text: One who goes round collecting for charity?

definitions.text: One who goes round collecting for charity?

parts.words: One who goes round collecting for charity?
parts.note: a member of a club named for its rotating meeting places, which raises money for good causes, is cast as someone who goes round

explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Rotary club, a service organisation, are known for charitable fundraising, and rotary means going round.

clue.text: Country lane crawling with CID

indicators.note: crawling with suggests the letters swarm into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A country road is full of plain-clothes police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crawling with' rearranges LANE and CID, the Criminal Investigation Department of British police.
explanation.definitionFit: Iceland is an island nation in the North Atlantic.

clue.text: Battle jacket protects medic

indicators.note: protects says one piece wraps round another

parts.note: a coat is a jacket
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor

explanation.surface: A combat jacket shields a medical officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battle jacket' reads as a real garment, which hides the split between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Combat is fighting, synonymous with battle.

clue.text: Disgraced boxer possibly found here

definitions.meaning: out of favour, in trouble with someone
a boxer is a breed of dog, which may sleep in a kennel

explanation.definitionFit: To be in the doghouse is the idiom for being in disgrace, and a dog's kennel is literally a dog house.

clue.text: Topple out of bed and come to a halt

parts.note: up means out of bed
to end is to come to a stop

explanation.surface: Someone falls out of bed and stops.
explanation.definitionFit: To upend something is to turn it over, topple it.

clue.text: Extremely versatile, really, to outward appearances

indicators.note: outward appearances points at the outside letters of each word

explanation.surface: Something seems wonderfully adaptable on the face of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the first and last letters of 'versatile' and 'really'.
explanation.definitionFit: Very means to a high degree, extremely.

clue.text: Thanks to soldiers, ,one's dressed in special headgear

indicators.note: dressed in says one piece is clothed by another, put inside it

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks
one is the Roman numeral I
RA is the Royal Artillery, a body of soldiers

explanation.surface: Thanking the troops, someone puts on a crown for the occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British informal for thanks and RA the Royal Artillery; the stray comma before 'one's' is the page's printing slip.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled ornamental band worn on the head on special occasions.

clue.text: Stiff upper lip Sue features, we're told

annotationWithheld.clue: Stiff upper lip Sue features, we're told

clue.text: Withdraw asylum

definitions.meaning: to pull back, as an army does
a refuge or place of shelter

explanation.definitionFit: Retreat is a verb for pulling back and a noun for a quiet place of refuge or sanctuary.

clue.text: One entitled to accompany attorney to Yankee festival

parts.note: a lady holds a title
DA is a district attorney
Yankee is Y in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A titled woman goes with a lawyer to an American celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: LADY DAY is the Feast of the Annunciation on 25 March, an old English quarter day.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Day is a church feast day honouring the Virgin Mary, hence a festival.
